It is voluntary evidence of practice, not a CISA Secure Software Development Attestation Form; no such form has been filed.

packages.summary: Single-file, fully offline HTML application that compiles DoD RMF control evidence from Tenable/ACAS scan exports.
packages.description: Palisade compiles STIG applicability, eMASS hardware and software baselines, PPSM registry rows, POA&M drafts, account audits and asset inventories from Tenable/ACAS scan exports. It is one HTML file opened from file:// on an air-gapped or NIPR workstation. There is no build step, no dependency, no network call and no browser storage.
packages.comment: Package scope is the distributed artifact only: the single file palisade.html. Repository documentation (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, docs/) and release-verification tooling are not shipped to the user and are excluded, which is what makes packageVerificationCode reproducible from the one file listed below. No CPE is asserted: Palisade has no entry in the NVD CPE dictionary, and inventing one would imply a registration that does not exist. The purl above is the unique identifier.

files.comment: 759,147 bytes, UTF-8, LF line endings, no BOM. Contains exactly one <script> block of 665,876 bytes whose SHA-256 (sha256-nl/LOgN8ndRe7CK4XhTvWUnP51eo5YcSZmUIgwE0fCg=) is the file's own CSP script-src. The SHA1 above is present because SPDX 2.3 requires it on a file and because packageVerificationCode is derived from it; SHA-256 and stronger are the digests to rely on.

relationships.comment: NONE is an explicit assertion, not an absence of data: Palisade has no third-party dependencies of any kind. This is the SPDX equivalent of the CycloneDX "dependsOn": [] in palisade.cdx.json.

annotations.comment: Why this inventory lists no dependencies: there are none to list. The single file carries no bundled library, no vendored code, no CDN reference, no subresource-integrity attribute, no package-manager manifest and no external src or href. A reviewer can falsify that claim in seconds with the greps in docs/SBOM.md rather than taking this document's word for it.
